debt.title: India's external debt (quarterly, RBI releases)
debt.frequency: quarterly; RBI publishes the March and June quarters (~1 quarter lag); Sep/Dec quarters are released by the Ministry of Finance and are not included
debt.source: RBI press releases 'India's External Debt as at the end of ...'

rows.label: March 2022
rows.valuation: Excluding the valuation effect, external debt would have increased by US$ 58.8 billion instead of US$ 47.1 billion at end-March 2022 over end-March 2021.

rows.label: June 2022
rows.valuation: Excluding the valuation effect, external debt would have increased by US$ 11.9 billion instead of a decrease of US$ 2.5 billion at end-June 2022 over end-March 2022.

rows.label: March 2023
rows.valuation: Excluding the valuation effect, external debt would have increased by US$ 26.2 billion instead of US$ 5.6 billion at end-March 2023 over end-March 2022.

rows.label: June 2023
rows.valuation: Valuation effect due to the appreciation of the US dollar vis-à-vis the major currencies such as yen and SDR 2 amounted to US$ 3.1 billion.

rows.label: March 2024
rows.valuation: Valuation effect due to the appreciation of the US dollar vis-à-vis the Indian rupee and other major currencies such as yen, the euro and SDR 2 amounted to US$ 8.7 billion.

rows.label: June 2024
rows.valuation: Valuation effect due to the appreciation of the US dollar vis-à-vis the Indian rupee and other major currencies such as yen, the euro and SDR 2 amounted to US$ 3.0 billion during the quarter ended June 2024.

rows.label: March 2025
rows.valuation: Valuation effect due to the appreciation of the US dollar vis-à-vis the Indian rupee and other currencies amounted to US$ 5.3 billion.

rows.label: June 2025
rows.valuation: Excluding the valuation effect, external debt would have increased by US$ 6.2 billion instead of US$ 11.2 billion at end-June 2025 over end-March 2025.

rows.label: March 2026
rows.valuation: Valuation effect due to the appreciation of the US dollar vis-à-vis the Indian rupee and other major currencies amounted to US$ 24.6 billion.

rows.label: June 2026
rows.valuation: Excluding the valuation effect, external debt would have increased by US$ 16.4 billion instead of US$ 15.4 billion at end-June 2026 over end-March 2026.

debt.caveat: Currency shares are as stated in each release (first-published, may be revised later). The USD share includes US-dollar debt only; SDR allocations have no market INR rate and are converted as a USD-equivalent approximation.
